issues.description: Class name mismatch and malformed template file: the exercise expects a public class named 'Farm' (see problem statement UML and Solution's Farm.java), but the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares 'public class AnimalFarm' and contains duplicated/nested package and class declarations (syntax repeated at lines 10-17). This causes a naming inconsistency (file Farm.java must contain public class Farm) and also introduces broken/duplicated code that will prevent compilation and block students from implementing the required Farm API (animals list, constructor, getters/setters, addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong).
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the broken template with a single public class named 'Farm' in package de.tum.cit.ase. Remove duplicated 'package' and nested class declarations and ensure Farm.java declares: public class Farm { private List<Animal> animals; public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); } public List<Animal> getAnimals(); public void setAnimals(List<Animal>); public void addAnimal(Animal); public void feedAllAnimals(); public void singFarmSong(); } (method bodies may be stubs). Align signatures and visibility with the UML in the problem statement and the solution's Farm.java so students can compile and implement the exercise.
